english.title: Acquire / increase control over a UK authorised person before expiration of the assessment period
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), having given notice in writing to the appropriate regulator, namely the

(A)_[Financial Conduct]_
(B)_[Prudential Regulation]_

Authority, under section 178(1) of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 of your decision to

(C)_[acquire]_
(D)_[increase]_

control over a UK authorised person, made the acquisition to which the notice related before the expiry date of the assessment period, the regulator not having approved the acquisition or given a warning notice under section 189(4)(b)(i) or section 190A of the Act
english.legislation: Contrary to section 191F(2) and (8) of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000.

investigatoraction.description: Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 401 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 provides that proceedings for offences may be instituted in England and Wales only by the 'appropriate regulator' (either the Financial Conduct or the Prudential Regulation Authority) or the Secretary of State or by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions.
(ii) For the purpose of this offence, the appropriate regulator means -
(a) where the UK authorised person is a PRA-authorised person, the Prudential Regulation Authority;
(b) in any other case, the Financial Conduct Authority.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: A fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
